aspects.says: Field 4 counts minor units of the currency in field 49, so the amount is scaled by that currency's decimals, exactly, and an amount finer than the currency allows is refused.
basis: section:11.1. An Amount Counts Minor Units, and Its Currency Says How Many Make One

aspects.says: The mean hides answers that arrive after the terminal's timeout; the 99th percentile shows them, and each one becomes a reversal.
basis: section:11.3. Capacity Is Sized From the Busiest Second, and Judged by the Slowest Answers

aspects.says: Each destination gets its own limit of requests in flight, so a slow issuer cannot take the sessions of healthy ones.
basis: section:11.4. A Slow Destination Gets a Limit of Its Own, and Past It an Immediate 91

aspects.says: A card goes to the destination of the most specific entry that holds it, whatever the entry's length or its place in the table.
basis: section:11.2. A Card Goes to the Destination of Its Longest Matching Prefix

aspects.says: A double cannot hold most decimal amounts exactly, so a multiply-and-cast loses a minor unit.
basis: section:11.1. An Amount Counts Minor Units, and Its Currency Says How Many Make One

aspects.says: Reports, settlement files and batch work run outside the authorization path, which keeps only what decides the answer.
basis: section:11.3. Capacity Is Sized From the Busiest Second, and Judged by the Slowest Answers
aspects.reason: a design rule about where work runs, with no behaviour a deterministic test can observe

aspects.says: Routing tables are kept in memory and replaced whole, so a lookup sees one version of the table.
basis: section:11.2. A Card Goes to the Destination of Its Longest Matching Prefix

aspects.says: A request beyond the limit is answered at once with 91, an error, not a decline, and its place is given back however the request ends.
basis: section:11.4. A Slow Destination Gets a Limit of Its Own, and Past It an Immediate 91

aspects.says: Capacity comes from the busiest hour times the burst factor, and in-flight requests are that rate times the answer time.
basis: section:11.3. Capacity Is Sized From the Busiest Second, and Judged by the Slowest Answers
